title: Sunday Lessons
source: Midnight Bet — Integrated ARC II — Games People Play
paragraphs: Sunday morning began with three women taking control in three different rooms. Ananya said: “Stand.” Aarav stood. Meera said: “Phone away.” Kabir obeyed. Shalini said: “Look at me.” Dev did. None of the men joked about the similarity. They did not know. Ananya’s session was not officially a lesson. She had called it practice. Aarav had called it coffee. They ended up in her studio anyway. She wore jeans. No blazer. The change made the room feel less professional.

The soft fabric of her top sat close enough to her body that the shape of her breasts was clear when she moved. Hair down. Aarav noticed. “Problem?” He smiled. “No.” “Good.” Ananya placed two chairs close. “Today.” “No cards.” “No mock.” “Conversation.” Aarav sat.

“About?” “Why you told your friends you wanted to kiss someone outside the group.” He stared. “How do you know?” “Mira messaged me.” Aarav nearly choked. “What?” Ananya smiled. “Kidding.” He looked murderous. She laughed. “You are easy.” “Cruel.” “Maybe.” Then serious.

“Why did you tell them?” Aarav thought. “Because hiding you made the wanting feel like something I was ashamed of.” Ananya’s expression changed. “That is not what I expected.” “What did you expect?” “Jealousy bait.” Aarav laughed. “Maybe that too.” She smiled. Honesty again. Ananya leaned closer. The soft upper curves of her breasts pressed against the thin fabric of her top. The heat of her body reached him across the small space between the chairs.

“Do you regret telling them?” “No.” “Do you still want to kiss me?” Aarav answered: “Yes.” She looked at him. “Ask.” His pulse jumped. “Can I kiss you?” “Yes.” First kiss. Slow. The soft press of her mouth against his. The faint taste of her lipstick. The way her body leaned in for one full second before she pulled back. Ananya kept control by ending it first. Aarav smiled.

“You like stopping.” “I like choosing.” That line stayed with him. Meera’s session with Kabir used a whiteboard game. Correct answer: She asked a personal question. Wrong answer: He asked one. No grades. No penalties. Just curiosity. Kabir solved first. Meera asked:

“Rhea?” He smiled. “What about her?” “You kissed her.” Kabir froze. “How?” Meera looked pleased. “Your face at rehearsal.” He laughed. “Teacher.” “Answer.” “Yes.” Meera nodded. Jealousy moved through her. The soft fabric of her blouse shifted when she leaned against the desk. The outline of her breasts was clear. Kabir saw.

“Good?” She looked at him. “Do not enjoy it.” He smiled. “Impossible.” Kabir intentionally missed the next question. Meera caught it. “You wanted a question.” “Yes.” “Ask.” “Are you jealous?” Meera stared. Then: “Yes.” Kabir’s smile faded. Truth hotter than teasing. Next round. Correct. Meera asked:

“Tara?” Kabir went still. Now it was his turn. “How do you know everything?” “Rhea looked at her.” Meera smiled. “Women notice women noticing men.” Kabir thought. Then: “Yes.” Meera’s jealousy changed shape. Not ownership. Curiosity. “Do you want her?” Kabir:
“Maybe.” Meera leaned back. “And me?” Kabir looked directly. “Yes.” Her breath shifted. The soft rise of her chest under the blouse was clear. The session ended with a kiss. Not as reward.

After the board was erased. After the game was over. Kabir asked. Meera said yes. Then stopped at one. The soft press of her mouth against his. The faint heat of her body when she leaned in. The quiet control in the way she pulled back first. “Enough.” He nodded. “Teacher.” She smiled.

“Student.” The titles had become erotic shorthand. Shalini and Dev met at a café instead of studio. She had suggested public space. Good idea. Naina happened to walk past. Maybe. Dev saw her through glass. Naina waved. Shalini followed his gaze. “Her?” Dev nodded.

“Naina.” “She is beautiful.” Dev looked at Shalini. “You are not supposed to make this easier.” Shalini laughed. “Jealousy?” “Maybe.” Shalini leaned forward. The soft upper curves of her breasts pressed against the table edge through her top. “I do not own you.” Dev smiled.

“Everyone is learning that sentence.” She looked at him. “Do you want her?” “Yes.” “Do you want me?” Dev answered: “Yes.” Shalini’s cheeks warmed. Good. No kiss in public. Their fingers touched when both reached for sugar. Neither moved. The soft contact of skin against skin lasted a full second longer than needed. Naina saw from outside. She smiled. Then walked on. At noon, the six met for wedding errands. No deliberate erotic plan.

Still Sunday lessons followed. Aarav listened when Mira said: “Come here.” Too quickly. Mira noticed. “Ananya.” He smiled. “Maybe.” Kabir went quiet when Rhea said: “Stop joking.” Meera’s influence. Rhea noticed. Dev did not retreat when Naina stepped close. Shalini. Naina noticed. The tutors were inside the men’s bodies now. Not physically. Behaviourally. That made them part of the same story. At the market, Sana and Mehul joined.

Sana walked beside Aarav. The soft press of her arm against his when they stopped at a stall. Mira watched. Mehul beside Naina. His hand brushed her lower back when he guided her past a display. Dev watched. Rhea stayed between Kabir and Arjun for ten uncomfortable minutes. The heat of both men on either side of her. The memory of Arjun’s hand at her waist. The memory of Kabir’s mouth in the parking basement. Tara arrived later with Rohan.

Kabir’s attention split. Rhea noticed. Meera’s name appeared on Kabir’s phone. Tara noticed his smile. Now she was jealous of a woman she barely knew. Good. Neha asked everyone to choose fabrics. Normal task. Mira held a red dupatta against herself. The soft fabric against the curve of her breasts. The way it fell over her waist. Aarav looked. Mehul looked too. Mira caught both. Enjoyed both. Naina tried green. The colour against her skin. The short dress she wore underneath.

Dev looked. Mehul looked. Naina saw Sana seeing. Sana smiled. No scandal. Rhea held gold. The fabric against the soft upper curves of her breasts. Kabir looked. Arjun looked. Rhea felt both. The market had no erotic activity. The gaze did the work.

Later, family lunch. Tara sat opposite Kabir. Rohan beside her. Meera texted: Good work today. Kabir glanced. Tara noticed. “Teacher?” He looked up. “Yes.” Rhea heard. Arjun heard. Everyone now knew everyone’s outside threads enough to feel them. At another table, Shalini texted Dev: Public spaces are safer. Dev smiled. Naina leaned over. The soft press of her breast against his arm through the fabric.

“Safer from?” He locked phone. She laughed. Aarav’s phone buzzed. Ananya: You left your watch. Mira saw. “Comfort item?” Aarav froze. She smiled. “You have a face.” He laughed. The tutors had followed them into every room. Not as bodies. As residual heat. As changed behaviour. As jealousy that now had names. By the time the day ended, the six carried more than wedding errands. They carried the knowledge that the women outside the group were no longer outside the story.
The next rehearsal would force a cleaner question: what changes when the partner changes but the wanting does not?.
